program.section_heading: Psychology Associate in Arts for Transfer
outcomes: Demonstrate an understanding of the major concepts of behavior, theoretical perspectives, empirical findings, and historical trends in psychology. Assessment:Exams, quizzes, papers, research and presentations.

Upon successful completion of the program, the student will be able to organize and differentiate the major concepts, theoretical perspectives, empirical findings, and historical trends in psychology.

Demonstrate an understanding of basic research methods and information competency in obtaining relevant information about the science and profession of psychology. Assessment:Exams, quizzes, papers, research and presentations.
Upon successful completion of the program, the student will be able to select and implement research methods used in psychology, including research design, data analysis, and interpretation.

Exhibit an awareness of the ethical and professional factors related to the diversity of individuals and groups within the discipline of psychology. Assessment:Exams, quizzes, papers, research and presentations.
Upon successful completion of the program, the student will be able to articulate and apply psychological principles to individual, interpersonal, group and societal issues.
Upon successful completion of the program, the student will be able to distinguish between and execute the value of ethical behavior in all aspects of the science and practice of psychology.
